newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah declines on Timor issue, fixing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah declines on Timor issue, fixing.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah declined against the dollar in late trading on Thursday, dealers said.
They said the rupiah fell slightly at midday following reports of fresh disturbances in east Timor.
"But it was knocked down again later in the afternoon after the central bank surprised the market with another depreciation of the rupiah," one local bank dealer said.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate to 2,332/2,524 and the conversion rate to 2,332/2,380 on Thursday.
Dealers said offshore response to the disturbance in east Timor was brief and failed to get any follow-through.
They said the real surprise was the fixing which seemed to surprise the market.

"We didn't really expect another higher fixing today. But the central bank had caught the market by surprise. It seems that the underlying tone on the dollar apppears to be slightly upbeat for now," the local bank dealer said.
Dealers said local operators were not really surprised as they had countered offshore dollars buying.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,333.5/34.00 at 1025 GMT against an opening of 2,332.5/33.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,333.0/33.50 and 2,330.80/31.00, respectively.
The local bank dealer said ample rupiah liquidity also seemed to have helped a dollar rebound.
Overnight swap was at 0.25/0.30. Tom/next swap fell to 1.0/1.5 points from 1.5 points in the morning, suggesting anticipation of further flush rupiah supply.
Dealers said swap rates remained soft on the back of ample liquidity in the money market.
One-month swap was at 15.75/16.50, two at 33.0/34.0, three at 49.5/51.0 and six at 97.0/98.0 points.
